disclaimer: These are implementation scenarios and predictions, not evidence. Magnitudes require modeling, pilots, and measurement before publication-grade claims.
organizing_hypothesis: System-level Constitutional Capitalism implemented gradually over 10–20 years could broaden ownership and renew middle-class resilience more than isolated tax changes; this remains unproven.
greatest_risk: Attempting too much too quickly across interconnected markets, retirement systems, trade, governance, and taxation.

scenarios.label: Years 1–3: Structural groundwork
possible_noticeable_effects: somewhat higher take-home pay if labor taxes fall
more public discussion of ownership and local investment

scenarios.label: Years 3–7: Middle-class rebuilding becomes visible
possible_mechanisms: lower taxes on ordinary labor increasing household cash flow
larger retirement ownership of productive assets
fewer community collapses after employer exit
illustrative_not_modeled_ranges: workers might keep an additional $4,000–$8,000/year if labor tax relief is designed that way — illustrative only, not a scored estimate
possible_outcomes: median household wealth rising faster than GDP

scenarios.label: Years 7–15: Ownership compounding
scenarios.thesis: Wages support life; ownership builds independence. Multiple ownership channels can compound in ways wages alone do not.

scenarios.label: Years 10–20: Ownership-based middle class (conditional)
scenarios.conditional_success_description: Historians might describe success less as a new tax system and more as a shift from a wage-based middle class to an ownership-based middle class.
scenarios.psychological_shift: Workers increasingly see themselves as builders of capital, not only earners of wages.

domain_outlooks.prediction: Extreme top-share concentration could moderate over time if new wealth accrues more broadly; median household wealth could rise; lower-middle resilience could improve.
Largest plausible effect is reducing chronic/intergenerational poverty via asset ownership, not overnight elimination of poverty.
GDP need not fall; well-designed broadening could support demand stability and entrepreneurship. Poor design could slow growth via compliance costs or investment deterrence.
If rules scale responsibilities with firm scale, local entrepreneurship and rural vitality could strengthen.
Most large firms would adapt rather than disappear; evaluation criteria may expand beyond quarterly earnings.
